title: 2nd Mystery The Ease Of Essential Power

questions.question: What is Allah’s power compared to at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It is compared to the purest and brightest light.

questions.question: What are the inner parts of created things compared to?
questions.answer: They are compared to shining mirrors.

questions.question: Which things are said to obey Allah’s command in this passage?
questions.answer: Everything, from tiny atoms to plants, animals, stars, suns, and moons.

questions.question: Why does the passage say making many things is easy for Allah?
questions.answer: Because all things obey His power, and nothing is hard for Him.

questions.question: When many things are created, what happens to Allah’s other tasks?
questions.answer: Nothing gets mixed up, and one task does not block another.

questions.question: For Allah’s power, how are big and small things different?
questions.answer: They are not different in difficulty.

questions.question: What example shows that a very large thing can move easily?
questions.answer: A huge ship can move as easily as a child moves a toy.

questions.question: What helps that ship move so easily in the example?
questions.answer: Order, balance, and obedience to command.

questions.question: In the army example, what can a commander send with one order?
questions.answer: He can send one soldier or a whole army.

questions.question: What does the army example teach about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: One command can direct many just as easily as one.

questions.question: In the balance example, what small thing is placed on one side?
questions.answer: A walnut.

questions.question: What surprising result happens in the balance example with the mountains?
questions.answer: One mountain goes up and the other goes down.

questions.question: What does the balance example help us understand?
questions.answer: Even very huge things can be moved by a wise law with ease.

questions.question: What two qualities of Allah’s power are named as the source of order and balance?
questions.answer: Divine justice and endless wisdom.

questions.question: What does Allah move as easily as atoms, according to the passage?
questions.answer: The stars.

questions.question: In spring, what does Allah give life to with one command?
questions.answer: A single fly and also the whole kind of flies, along with many plants and animals.

questions.question: What big event in nature is compared to bringing a tree back to life?
questions.answer: Bringing the earth back to life in spring.

questions.question: How many kinds of springtime revivals does the passage mention on the earth?
questions.answer: Hundreds of thousands.

questions.question: What is one main idea of this passage?
questions.answer: Allah creates and gives life to many great and small things with the same ease.

questions.question: What picture does the passage use for Allah’s eternal power?
questions.answer: A very pure and shining light.

questions.question: How are created things described because they can receive that power?
questions.answer: They are described like bright mirrors.

questions.question: Name three kinds of things that obey Allah in the passage.
questions.answer: Atoms, animals, and stars.

questions.question: What does the passage say about creating one thing and creating countless things?
questions.answer: Both are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: If Allah is caring for many things, does one job delay another?
questions.answer: No, one does not interrupt another.

questions.question: Which pairs are said to be the same for Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Big and small, many and few, and single and universal.

questions.question: What everyday example is used to help us picture easy movement?
questions.answer: A child pushing a toy.

questions.question: What very large object is compared with that toy?
questions.answer: A huge ship.

questions.question: What does the ship example teach about Allah’s way of acting?
questions.answer: His power works through order and control.

questions.question: In the next example, who gives one command?
questions.answer: A commander.

questions.question: With the same kind of command, what two sizes of group can be sent?
questions.answer: One foot soldier or a whole army.

questions.question: What does that show about numbers and power?
questions.answer: Many can be directed as easily as one.

questions.question: In the scale example, what giant things are on the balance?
questions.answer: Two mountains.

questions.question: What small object changes the balance in the example?
questions.answer: One walnut.

questions.question: What lesson does the mountain scale example give?
questions.answer: A small cause, under a wise rule, can move very large things.

questions.question: What are the roots of order and regularity in creation, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s justice and wisdom.

questions.question: What heavenly bodies are said to move easily by Allah’s order?
questions.answer: The stars.

questions.question: What living things are mentioned when the passage talks about springtime life?
questions.answer: A fly, all flies, plants, and animals.

questions.question: What does Allah do to the earth in spring?
questions.answer: He brings it back to life like a resurrection.

questions.question: How hard is that spring revival for Allah?
questions.answer: It is done with the greatest ease.

questions.question: At the beginning of the passage, what is special about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It is described as the finest and brightest light.

questions.question: Why are things compared to mirrors in this passage?
questions.answer: Because they receive and show the work of Allah’s power.

questions.question: Does the passage speak only about small things obeying Allah, or small and great things both?
questions.answer: It speaks about both small and great things.

questions.question: Give one tiny thing and one huge thing named in the passage.
questions.answer: An atom and a sun.

questions.question: What makes it natural that many things can be created together?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is perfect, and all things submit to His command.

questions.question: When many things are placed side by side, what problem does the passage say does not happen?
questions.answer: Their creation does not interfere with each other.

questions.question: For Allah’s power, are few and many treated differently?
questions.answer: No, they are the same.

questions.question: What large object is moved in the first example after this main idea?
questions.answer: A very large ship.

questions.question: What small action is it compared to?
questions.answer: A child moving a toy with a finger.

questions.question: Which qualities make that comparison possible in the passage?
questions.answer: Order, balance, obedience, and submission.

questions.question: In the commander example, what remains the same when the number increases?
questions.answer: The single command.

questions.question: What does that tell us about Allah’s command?
questions.answer: One command is enough for many as well as one.

questions.question: In the balance story, what are the two very heavy things?
questions.answer: Two mountains.

questions.question: What happens to them when the balance changes?
questions.answer: One rises and the other lowers.

questions.question: What does the passage say is found in Allah’s power and leads to order in creation?
questions.answer: Justice and endless wisdom.

questions.question: What does Allah move easily in the sky?
questions.answer: The stars.

questions.question: What does Allah revive in spring besides one fly?
questions.answer: The whole kind of flies and many plants and animals.

questions.question: How is reviving the earth in spring like reviving a tree?
questions.answer: Both are done by Allah easily with wise power.

questions.question: What does the springtime earth look like in this passage?
questions.answer: It looks like something dead brought back to life.

questions.question: What is a good short summary of the whole passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s power controls everything with perfect order, and nothing is difficult for Him.

questions.question: What image is used for the true nature of created things?
questions.answer: They are like shining mirrors.

questions.question: Which list best matches the passage: only living things, or living and nonliving things too?
questions.answer: Both living and nonliving things.

questions.question: What are some nonliving things named that obey Allah?
questions.answer: Atoms, stars, suns, and moons.

questions.question: What are some living things named that obey Allah?
questions.answer: Plants and animals.

questions.question: What does the passage say about creating countless things and one thing?
questions.answer: There is no difference in ease for Allah.

questions.question: If Allah handles many matters at once, what happens between those matters?
questions.answer: They do not get in each other’s way.

questions.question: What very big thing is mentioned as moving forward easily?
questions.answer: A ship as large as many houses.

questions.question: What small picture is used to help a child understand that motion?
questions.answer: A toy being pushed by a child’s finger.

questions.question: What can be sent with one command besides one soldier?
questions.answer: A whole army.

questions.question: What is the main lesson from the soldier and army example?
questions.answer: The same command can direct one or many.

questions.question: In the scale example, what is balanced before the small object is added?
questions.answer: Two mountains.

questions.question: What tiny object tips the balance in the example?
questions.answer: A walnut.

questions.question: What does this example show about size under Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Even the largest things are easy to control.

questions.question: Which two qualities are said to be behind order and balance in creation?
questions.answer: Wisdom and justice.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does Allah move as easily as the tiniest parts?
questions.answer: The stars.

questions.question: In spring, what group of living things is especially named along with flies?
questions.answer: Plants and animals.

questions.question: What happens to the earth in spring in this passage?
questions.answer: It is raised from a dead state to life.

questions.question: How does the passage describe Allah doing all this?
questions.answer: With the greatest ease.

questions.question: What is the first big idea given about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It is pure, bright, and perfect like the highest light.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention mirrors?
questions.answer: To show that created things can display Allah’s power.

questions.question: From the smallest to the largest, who obeys Allah in this passage?
questions.answer: Everything in creation obeys Him.

questions.question: What does this obedience help explain about creation?
questions.answer: It explains why many things can be made as easily as one.

questions.question: What happens when many things are created at the same time?
questions.answer: Nothing clashes and no task blocks another.

questions.question: What three comparisons are used to show Allah’s equal power over all things?
questions.answer: Great and small, many and few, and single and universal.

questions.question: What huge object is used in the first example after that?
questions.answer: A giant ship.

questions.question: What tiny action is used to compare with moving that ship?
questions.answer: A child pushing a toy.

questions.question: What words in the passage explain why this is possible?
questions.answer: Order, balance, obedience, and submission.

questions.question: In the next example, what does one command do for a commander?
questions.answer: It can send one soldier or an entire army.

questions.question: Why is that example important in the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that one and many are equally easy to direct.

questions.question: What are placed in the two sides of the balance in the mountain example?
questions.answer: Two mountains.

questions.question: What little item changes the balance?
questions.answer: A walnut.

questions.question: What can we infer from that example about Allah’s rule over creation?
questions.answer: His wise laws can control huge things very easily.

questions.question: What begins all order and regularity in creation, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s justice and endless wisdom.

questions.question: Which is easier for Allah: moving atoms or moving stars?
questions.answer: Both are equally easy.

questions.question: In spring, what does Allah do to one fly?
questions.answer: He gives it life.

questions.question: What else does Allah bring to life with that same ease?
questions.answer: The whole kind of flies and all the groups of plants and animals.

questions.question: What large dead-looking thing becomes alive again in spring?
questions.answer: The earth.

questions.question: What does the passage compare spring on earth to?
questions.answer: A resurrection.

questions.question: How is Allah’s power described at the start of the target passage?
questions.answer: As the most delicate and shining light.

questions.question: What does the passage say created things are like inside?
questions.answer: They are like bright mirrors.

questions.question: Which range of creation is mentioned as obeying Allah?
questions.answer: From atoms and plants to animals and heavenly bodies.

questions.question: What does their obedience show about Allah creating many things?
questions.answer: It shows that making many things is just as easy as making one.

questions.question: When Allah does many things, what does not happen?
questions.answer: One work does not disturb another.

questions.question: What opposite sizes are named as equal before Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Large and small.

questions.question: What opposite amounts are also named as equal?
questions.answer: Many and few.

questions.question: What big vehicle is mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: A very large ship.

questions.question: What child-sized object is used to explain its movement?
questions.answer: A toy.

questions.question: What does the ship example say about how Allah’s power works?
questions.answer: It works through perfect order and control.

questions.question: In the commander example, what two choices are sent by one order?
questions.answer: One soldier or a whole army.

questions.question: What does that teach about Allah’s command?
questions.answer: A single command is enough for all.

questions.question: In the balance example, what enormous things stand on the scale?
questions.answer: Two mountains.

questions.question: What small thing is added to one side?
questions.answer: One walnut.

questions.question: What happens after that in the example?
questions.answer: One side rises and the other side falls.

questions.question: Which qualities of Allah are named as the source of order and balance?
questions.answer: His justice and wisdom.

questions.question: What does Allah move in space as easily as tiny particles?
questions.answer: The stars.

questions.question: What does Allah do to flies, plants, and animals in spring?
questions.answer: He gives them life and sends them into living existence.

questions.question: What does Allah do to the earth in spring?
questions.answer: He revives it after it was like a corpse.

questions.question: How easy is all of this for Allah, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It is done with complete ease.
